kind: User-supplied diagnostics and local code review; no account access or actual cloud health upload
interpretation: The last command made zero health uploads; its oldest pending target had already consumed its extra recovery allowance.
READBACK_UNVERIFIED alone cannot distinguish an accepted response from transport uncertainty, and does not establish explicit rejection.
The existing recovery ledger retains accepted, businessCode and readbackStatus, but version .8 omitted those fields from its report.
legacy_row_metadata_unknown describes the original pending journal's absent outer timezone metadata; recovery sends the current validated offset.
A complete missing history result is not evidence that replay is idempotent or that the original request never applied. Increasing preflight page limits alone does not solve the reported case.
confirmed_code_gaps_and_changes: Post-upload recovery previously queried only ordinary windows. The new fallback reads native history once after three unsuccessful windows, with a 32-page bound and no additional upload.
All observations of the target from post-upload queries are combined so later matches or exceptions cannot erase a tombstone, other source or content conflict.
Incomplete native absence is classified before persistence as UNQUERIED; it is never transiently saved as MISSING.
Authentication failure after submission remains inside the recovery runner to prevent a whole-operation retry.
Read-only recovery of an existing match now uses the journal's atomic pending-snapshot reconciliation, without granting uploaded ownership.

Both the single-recovery report and read-only reconciliation expose allowlisted previous metadata. Reconciliation chooses the same oldest pending target as recovery and never advances to another target to borrow its history.
limits: Synthetic regression tests validate client behavior; they do not prove these 133 user-account records can be recovered.
No device is attached, no real account is accessed and no phone instrumentation is run.
The exhausted target is not uploaded again by this release. The next read-only report can reveal the already-stored prior response but cannot reconstruct evidence never persisted.
No new proven SpO2 wire-encoding defect or server-side idempotency guarantee was established.
